crm_notes:
Summary: Financial analytics platform. High-sensitivity PII+transaction data. Strong preference for Private VPC deployment with customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed envelopes. CISO team leading security review; primary concerns are key custody, attestation, and audit forwarding to Splunk.

Key quotes: "We cannot hand over raw keys or lose chain-of-custody — need BYOK and HSM attestation", CISO M. Kovac.

KMS/HSM requirements (from call):
- Support AWS KMS + CloudHSM for primary region (eu-west-1)
- Fallback to Azure Key Vault (with Managed HSM) for DR across eu-north-1
- GCP KMS acceptable only for analytics sandboxes, not prod
- BYOK import flow: customer wraps root key (RSA-4096) and Redwood must support envelope encryption and rotate TEKs without exposing root key material
- Hardware attestation: need vendor-signed evidence (FIPS 140-2/3 Level 3 or equivalent) and EC2 Nitro enclave attestation details where used
- Audit: export of key usage logs to customer SIEM (Syslog/Splunk) + immutable audit trail retention 7+ years

Integration notes from SE workshop:
- Proposed architecture: keys in customer KMS, Redwood uses EEK (encrypted envelope keys) pattern; runtime retrieves short-lived TEKs via KMS Decrypt (GRPC) and stores only in volatile memory on inference host
- Network: VPC peering + strict egress allowlist; option to host control-plane proxy in customer VPC for handshake to reduce external network dependencies
- Rotation: automated TEK rotation every 7 days; master key rotation per customer policy, Redwood supports re-wrapping without downtime (can demonstrate in PoC)

POC scope agreed:
- Demonstrate AWS KMS BYOK import + CloudHSM-backed CMK for production inference
- Show audit log forward to Meridian Splunk test index (sample dashboard)
- Validate key attestation artifacts and provide an attestation checklist for Legal

Docs/Artifacts: Security Workbook v2 (drive link), initial architecture diagram (attached in drive), short demo recording (ff id).
